penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: WordPress SMB owners are essentially individual consumers in purchasing behavior — low average revenue per user, high churn, and the business model only works at volume (hundreds of paying users) which a solo factory cannot reach organically.

rationale: The buyer is a small business owner managing their own WordPress site — technically a business, but in practice a consumer-grade buyer who expects cheap or free SEO tools and has many existing free options (Yoast free tier, RankMath, custom PHP snippets). Willingness to pay for a narrow dynamic-page SEO title fix is low, the problem is mild rather than blocking, and the market requires scale to generate meaningful revenue. There is no clear autonomous delivery mechanism — this would be a WordPress plugin or a one-off consulting fix, neither of which fits the factory model well.
solution_plan: Not viable as a factory service in its current form. The pattern of 'WordPress users struggling with plugin limitations on dynamic pages' is worth watching — if aggregated across dozens of similar queries it might point to a specific niche (e.g. directory site owners) where pain is sharper and willingness to pay is higher. No action recommended now.
notes: Dropped. Signal strength is 1 (single StackExchange question). build_gate failures: buyer_clarity (4, floor 6), willingness_to_pay (4, floor 5). Revisit if pattern recurs with stronger buyer signals.
